Inspection Findings: 

Raw materials are given a fixed 2-year shelf life from receipt (unless shorter is stated by the manufacturer), without documented scientific justification, stability data, or formal risk assessment covering storage, repackaging, or handling conditions.

Higher-risk manufacturers may not receive enhanced assurance activities (e.g. audits or additional testing), reducing confidence in GMP compliance and supply chain risk control.

Certain higher-risk excipients linked to historical DEG/EG contamination (e.g. glycerol, propylene glycol, low molecular weight PEGs) are used on site, with no documented risk assessment or enhanced supplier/incoming verification strategy in place.

Inspection Findings: 

Manufacturer qualification and supply chain assurance require strengthening. Qualification activities focus on distributors/wholesalers rather than the actual manufacturing sites. 

Suppliers operating outside the UK/EEA are identified as higher risk; however, additional qualification activities, equivalence assessments and enhanced controls are not clearly defined or consistently applied.

Supplier requalification frequency does not align with the current SOP. SOP 011 requires annual reassessment; however, suppliers are currently reassessed every two years.

The updated guide to defective medicinal products was published by MHRA on the 16th February 2026.

The following are the relevant updates that will be integrated into our procedures: 

Contact details specified between normal working hours and out of hours. 
Initial impact assessments now expected to include proposed market action/containment (recall, quarantine or other mitigating containment actions)
Guidance now stipulates that all Class 1 Medicines Recalls, will be issued as National Patient Safety Alerts.

APSM – Key Points (25th February 2026)

Home Office CD licensing: The Home Office has recruited more licensing staff and is considering improved applicant updates. The Home Office identified maintaining valid DBS clearance throughout the application process as a major cause of licensing delays.

CBPM policy: APSM raised the need for clearer MHRA policy and guidance for cannabis-based medicinal products.
 
MHRA engagement: APSM can submit agenda items to raise practical issues affecting CBPMs, Schedule 1 imports, specials manufacturing or regulatory guidance for the June 2026 MHRA Partnership Group meeting.

Quarter Summary
The Pharmaceutical Quality System remained stable and effective throughout the review period. Review of quality metrics indicates no adverse trends requiring escalation or additional management intervention.

Key observations include:
No emerging trends identified within deviations, complaints, OOS/OOT investigations or returned products.
CAPAs continue to be completed within established timeframes, with no significant backlog observed.
Extensions for Change Controls and Risk Assessments remain low.
Overall document closure performance remains satisfactory, all documents completed within their assigned due dates.
No overdue quality records of significant regulatory or business concern were identified during the review period.

Key Risks

Business Central (BC) Recall Traceability & Reconciliation
Current Risk Level: Medium
Proposed Actions:
Targeted QA training focused on product traceability and recall functionality within BC
Review whether required information for recall management can be obtained through a single reporting process.
Assess opportunities to improve reporting functionality and reduce reliance on manual data extraction.
Verify effectiveness during a future mock recall and traceability activities.

Controlled Document Backlog
Current Risk Level: Low-Medium
Proposed Actions:
Continue prioritisation of overdue document review activities.
Monitor backlog reduction through routine Quality Management review.
Escalate resource requirements if progress stalls.

Key Improvements Achieved

Successful management and closure of Quetiapine recall, with full product accountability and reconciliation achieved.
Significant enhancement of the Scientific Rationale process, strengthening GMP decision-making and regulatory compliance.
Continued reduction in overdue controlled documentation.
No Manufacturing rejected batches recorded during the review period.
